description: A 2HP version of FancyBox: the same six background layers with their options in dialogs, and no control voltage inputs

params.text: Turns the colour wash layer on and off
Turns the linear gradient layer on and off
Turns the radial gradient layer on and off
Turns the box gradient, the vignette, on and off
Turns the background picture layer on and off
Switches the whole background on and off
Turns the cases layer on and off, drawing a frame and a drop shadow around each unbroken run of modules

notes: nothing is drawn until the background is switched on; every layer stays hidden and the blue lamp stays dark until then
a layer's own check box has to be ticked as well; only the colour wash is ticked on a new module
the picture layer shows nothing until an image file is chosen, whatever the check box says
a colour input is only read while its layer is ticked and that colour's fade is above zero
a fast, full-range signal on these inputs gives flashing results; a bipolar signal through an attenuator, with the knobs set part way, gives a gentler one
only one FancyBox works at a time, counting the mini: a second one added to the patch is drawn greyed out with no controls on it at all
the six layers are drawn one over another in this order: picture, colour wash, linear gradient, radial gradient, vignette, cases
the cases layer draws a frame and a drop shadow around each unbroken run of modules; a module standing on its own gets no case, and a gap of more than 1HP starts a new one
every setting other than these switches is in the dialogs behind the hamburger marks, one per layer; those settings have no control on the panel, so no click on the module reaches help for them
the module underneath is the one FancyBox uses, so the same background can be built here; this panel leaves out all 46 control voltage inputs, and none of them can be patched
menu: Keep effects when removed — leaves the background in place after this module is deleted from the patch; the settings are then lost when the patch is unloaded, so save a preset first
